candidates.api_shape: parallel_gripper(stroke, jaw_w, drive='rack'|'screw', open_frac) -> {body, jaw_a, jaw_b, drive}
candidates.fdm: Two jaws on opposing slides, a rack-and-pinion or a leadscrew between them. Prints. Pose is open_frac. Fingers are arguments, not a second kit. The robot 2-finger default (Schunk PGN / Robotiq 2F class as a semi-primitive, not a product clone).
candidates.name: parallel_gripper
candidates.why: Two jaws translate toward a midplane and stay parallel. Pick-and-place, vises that ride a robot, every cobot EOAT request. No current API closes two jaws in parallel. iris and scroll centre; toggle and cam press; none of them is a parallel gripper.

candidates.fdm: Two jaws on pivots, a cam or a link spreads them. Prints flat. Cheaper and shorter than parallel. Not a toggle (which presses a toe to a table).
candidates.name: angular_gripper
candidates.why: Pivoting 2-jaw. The other named robot gripper. Wider opening, jaws do not stay parallel. Distinct from toggle_clamp (workholding press) and from parallel_gripper.

candidates.api_shape: draw_latch(reach, overcenter_deg, strap_w) -> {base, hasp, hook} posed locked/open
candidates.fdm: A hinged hasp that pulls a hook over-center. Prints flat. Chest, flight case, enclosure. 507-adjacent to toggle.
candidates.name: draw_latch
candidates.why: Over-center latch that draws two panels together. toggle_clamp presses a part to a table; snap_catch is a lid finger. A draw latch is the missing panel-to-panel lock.

candidates.api_shape: machine_vise(jaw_w, opening, screw_d, close_frac) -> {body, moving_jaw, screw, ways}
candidates.fdm: Fixed jaw + moving jaw on a way + trapezoidal screw. Prints. Soft jaws are a swap-in. The handle and the Kurt angle-lock are product extras.
candidates.name: machine_vise
candidates.why: The bench/mill vise. lead_screw's usecase names vices but there is no jaw pair or way. Distinct from a gripper (no robot flange) and from a collet (on-axis).

candidates.api_shape: hood_latch(hook_r, overcenter_deg) -> {hook, striker, handle} posed locked
candidates.fdm: A hook that catches a striker and goes over-center. Prints. Car-hood / crate class. toggle_clamp kinematics, hook instead of a press toe.
candidates.name: hood_latch
candidates.why: Over-center hook latch. The prompt listed it. Not a draw (which pulls a hasp) and not a toggle clamp (which presses). Same over-center law, different job.

candidates.api_shape: soft_jaw(stock, pocket_2d or bore, bolt_pattern) -> a consumable insert
candidates.fdm: A block with a part-shaped pocket and two bolt holes. The thing people reprint per job. Not a vise.
candidates.name: soft_jaw
candidates.why: Sacrificial vise/chuck insert. The FDM workholding people actually search. A pocket in a brick, not a new mechanism. Still a named primitive so agents stop inventing it from boxc.

candidates.api_shape: pawl_latch(striker, pawl, spring) -> slam / rotary catch
candidates.fdm: A sprung pawl and a striker. Prints. Door slam, rotary glove-box, toolbox. snap_catch is a lid finger; this is a load-bearing catch.
candidates.name: pawl_latch
candidates.why: Pawl/slam latch. The prompt listed latch/pawl catch. Distinct from snap_catch (light lid) and from a ratchet (one-way drive).

candidates.fdm: A flat lip + a barb. TPU. bellows_suction_cup is the folded sibling. Oval is an argument.
candidates.name: flat_vacuum_cup
candidates.why: The other vacuum family. Flat cups for smooth sheets; bellows for uneven. Only bellows exists. A kind= on one cup API is enough.

candidates.fdm: A slotted strap, a heel step, a stud. Prints. Mill-table default. No over-center; the stud is the force.
candidates.name: toe_clamp
candidates.why: Strap / toe / step clamp. The workholding that is not a toggle and not a cam. Every mill fixture.

candidates.api_shape: compose scroll_drive + three finger bodies; do not add a second scroll
candidates.fdm: scroll_drive already closes three jaws equally. Fingers are attachments.
candidates.name: three_finger
candidates.why: 3-finger centric robot gripper. The mechanism is scroll_drive (usecase already says three-jaw). A finger kit is composition.

candidates.api_shape: a C frame plus lead_screw and a pad
candidates.name: c_clamp
candidates.why: C-clamp. lead_screw plus a frame. After machine_vise, low leverage.

candidates.fdm: ISO tool-changer plates are products. Dock is the locate primitive.
candidates.name: atc_plate
candidates.why: repeatable_dock's usecase already names tool changers. Do not add a Schunk/ATI clone.

candidates.name: magnetic_chuck
candidates.why: Bought magnets or an electromagnet. Same reject as magnetic_gear / magnetic_clutch.

candidates.name: scroll_again
candidates.why: Already the self-centering 3-jaw mechanism. 3-finger robot is fingers on this.

rejected.name: schunk_pg_clone
rejected.why: A named pneumatic gripper with a specific body is a product. parallel_gripper is the semi-primitive.

rejected.name: kurt_vise_product
rejected.why: Angle-lock vise with a specific casting. machine_vise is the screw+jaws+way.

rejected.name: bernoulli_pad
rejected.why: Non-contact air levitation. Needs a compressor and a shaped nozzle; a project fixture.

rejected.name: compliant_tweezer_product
rejected.why: A finished living-hinge gripper. living_hinge (flexure slice) is the cell.

summary:
Holding splits by what is being held and how the force is made. Chucks centre a round part on an axis (scroll, collet, 4-jaw). Workholding clamps a part to a table (toggle, cam, vise, strap/toe). Robot grippers pick a free part (parallel jaw, angular, 3-finger, vacuum, magnetic). Latches hold two panels shut (draw, hood/over-center, slam/pawl, snap). 507 names bench clamps 174/180/381, screw clamp 190, toggle 140. Norton treats vises and chucks as screw-and-wedge. Howell's holding is a compliant tweezer or a living-hinge clip, not a Schunk jaw.

Catalog already covers the clamp/chuck/locate staples and one vacuum cup. Over-center: toggle_clamp (knee linkage, posed), eccentric_cam_clamp (eccentric disc + follower, posed). On-axis chuck: collet_chuck (split taper + nut), scroll_drive (Archimedean rib + three jaws, the self-centering 3-jaw mechanism). Vacuum: bellows_suction_cup. Aperture: iris_diaphragm. Locate: kinematic_coupling, repeatable_dock (usecase already says tool changers), three_point_leveller. Lid snaps: snap_catch / snap_finger. lead_screw's usecase names vices. Grep finds no parallel-jaw gripper, angular gripper, draw latch, hood latch, machine vise, soft-jaw insert, pawl/slam latch, flat vacuum cup, or strap/toe clamp. The grippers shelf blurb is 'Parts that hold, centre, and grip' but the robot 2-finger primitive is missing.

FDM reality. Parallel-jaw gripper is two slides (or a parallelogram) driven by a rack-and-pinion or a leadscrew; the default robot EOAT and the highest-leverage missing kit. Angular gripper is two jaws on pivots (simpler, cheaper, not parallel). 3-finger centric is scroll_drive plus finger bodies, not a new scroll. Draw latch is an over-center hasp that pulls two panels together (chest, case, flight case). Hood latch is a striker hook that goes over-center (car hood, toggle_clamp kinematics on a hook, not a press toe). Machine vise is lead_screw + two jaws + a way; the product handle stays out. Soft jaw is a consumable insert with a part-shaped pocket, the thing people reprint. Pawl / slam latch is a sprung catch that a striker lifts and drops behind. Flat vacuum cup is the non-bellows sibling. Strap/toe clamp is a slotted bar + stud, the mill table default. Magnetic chucks and Bernoulli pads are hardware. A finished Schunk or a Kurt vise is a product.
title: Grippers, chucks, latches, and workholding
